grades.quote: By switching frequently between the runnable threads, if any one of them needs only a little processing time, it will get that time relatively soon even if the other threads involve long computations.
grades.reason: Explains why frequent switching improves responsiveness, but not why it reduces throughput.

grades.quote: Keeping the workload fixed, the experimenter varies the scheduler parameters and measures such performance indicators as response time and throughput. No one set of parameters will optimize all measures of performance for all workloads.
grades.reason: Provides general background on scheduler performance tradeoffs, but does not explain the effects of frequent context switches.

grades.quote: Each can subvert the prioritization of threads, and the convoy phenomenon can also greatly increase the context switching rate and hence decrease system throughput.
grades.reason: Directly links increased context switching to decreased throughput, but does not explain the responsiveness benefit.

grades.quote: High performance may mean high throughput (Section 3.3.1) or fast response time (Section 3.3.2), and user control may be expressed in terms of urgency, importance, or resource allocation (Section 3.3.3).
grades.reason: Identifies throughput and response time as scheduling goals, without explaining the context-switch tradeoff.
